mainTopic: The disputes of בית שמאי and בית הלל about מיאון, the גמרא's four explanations for why בית שמאי bar a married girl from refusing, and רבי אושעיא's rule on refusing a יבם's מאמר but not his זיקה.
overview: This amud deals with מיאון. When a girl's father has died, the חכמים allowed her mother or brothers to marry her off while she is still a קטנה, and she may later refuse that marriage and end it. The משנה lists four disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל: whether a נשואה can refuse, whether she can refuse a יבם, whether the husband must be present, and whether a בית דין is needed. In each one בית הלל is more lenient. The two schools then argue about whether she may refuse again and again, and בית שמאי say בנות ישראל are not הפקר. The גמרא gives four explanations for why בית שמאי do not let a married girl refuse. שמואל says people would think a marriage can have a תנאי. רבה and רב יוסף say a husband does not want his relations to turn into זנות. רב פפא says it is about the profits of her property. רבא says it is about the cost of the wedding feast. Each time, the גמרא also gives בית הלל's answer. Finally, רבי אושעיא rules that a girl can refuse a יבם's מאמר but not his זיקה. רב חסדא explains that she can undo what she agreed to but not what was forced on her, and the גמרא begins a challenge from ביאה, which can also happen against her will. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who may refuse: only betrothed girls, or married girls too?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say only ארוסות can do מיאון. בית הלל say both ארוסות and נשואות can.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: only betrothed girls may refuse. בית הלל say: both betrothed and fully married girls may refuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the first of four arguments about מיאון. This one is about which stage of marriage a girl can still refuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ארוסה has only had the first stage of marriage (אירוסין). A נשואה has completed the marriage (נישואין). בית שמאי limit מיאון to the first stage, while בית הלל allow it even after a full marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal: a girl married off as a minor declares she does not want the marriage, and this ends it.
Betrothed girls, who have done only the first stage of marriage (אֵירוּסִין).
Fully married girls, who have completed נִישּׂוּאִין.
The two great schools of תַּנָּאִים, who often disagree.

steps.confusionAlert: מיאון is not a גט (divorce). It is a special refusal that only works for a girl married off as a קטנה under rabbinic law.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
Only betrothed girls may refuse,
phrases.notes: This is about a girl whose father died and whose mother or brothers married her off while she was still a minor.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say:
both betrothed and fully married girls may refuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מְמָאֲנִין אֶלָּא אֲרוּסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: מיאון works only for ארוסות. בית הלל: it works for ארוסות and נשואות.

steps.title: Refusing the husband only, or also the יבם
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say מיאון works only against the husband, not the יבם. בית הלל say it works against both.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: she may refuse her husband but not her יבם. בית הלל say: she may refuse her husband or her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second argument. If the young husband died and she now falls to his brother (the יבם), can she use מיאון to get out of that bond?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, מיאון can only undo the marriage with the husband himself. Once she falls to a יבם, she would need חליצה to be released. בית הלל let her refuse the יבם too.

keyTerms.meaning: The brother of a man who died without children, who is bound to his widow (יִבּוּם).

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בַּבַּעַל וְלֹא בַּיָּבָם,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: she may refuse the husband but not the yavam,
and Beit Hillel say: the husband or the yavam.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בַּבַּעַל וְלֹא בַּיָּבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second dispute in the same series about מיאון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: מיאון works only against the husband. בית הלל: against the husband or the יבם.

steps.title: Must the refusal happen in front of him?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי require the מיאון to be said in the husband's presence. בית הלל allow it in his presence or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: in his presence. בית הלל say: in his presence or not in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third argument. It asks whether the husband has to be there when she refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי treat the refusal as something said to the husband's face. בית הלל say the refusal works even if he is not there.

keyTerms.meaning: In his presence, in front of him.
Not in his presence, when he is not there.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: in his presence,
phrases.notes: "His" means the husband she is refusing.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: בְּפָנָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: in his presence or not in his presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third dispute in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: מיאון must be in the husband's presence. בית הלל: it is valid even when he is absent.

steps.title: Must the refusal happen in court?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי require the מיאון to be in a בית דין. בית הלל allow it in a בית דין or outside one.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: in court. בית הלל say: in court or not in court.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth and last argument about how מיאון is done. It asks whether a בית דין is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again בית שמאי make the refusal more formal and בית הלל make it easier. For בית הלל, a refusal said outside a בית דין still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in court, outside a בית דין.

steps.whatToRemember: In all four arguments, בית שמאי restrict מיאון and בית הלל are lenient. בית הלל allow it for married girls, against a יבם, outside the husband's presence, and outside a בית דין.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: in court.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: בְּבֵית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: in court or not in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth and final dispute in the series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: מיאון must be in a בית דין. בית הלל: it is valid in or out of a בית דין.

steps.title: בית הלל: she may refuse many times while still a minor
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל tell בית שמאי that a קטנה may do מיאון again and again, even four or five times.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: she may refuse as long as she is a minor, even four or five times.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the two schools speak directly to each other. בית הלל state that a girl who is still a קטנה can refuse over and over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture this: she refuses one husband, her family marries her off again, and she refuses again. בית הלל say this can repeat as long as she is still a קטנה. This sets up בית שמאי's sharp reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They said to them. This opens a direct argument between the two sides.
A girl who has not yet reached halachic adulthood.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean she is married to several men at once. Each refusal ends the marriage before she is married off to the next man.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
She may refuse as long as she is a minor,
even four or five times.
phrases.notes: Each time, her family married her off again after she refused the last husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the four listed disputes to a direct debate between the schools.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: a קטנה may do מיאון repeatedly, even four or five times.

steps.title: בית שמאי: Jewish girls are not ownerless property
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי reject repeated refusals. They say בנות ישראל are not הפקר. She refuses, waits until she grows up, then refuses and marries.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: the daughters of Israel are not ownerless. Rather, she refuses and waits until she grows up, and then she refuses and marries.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back against בית הלל's view. They object to a girl being passed from man to man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling them "not הפקר" means girls should not be treated like ownerless objects that anyone can pick up and drop. So instead of many marriages and refusals while she is young, בית שמאי say she must wait until she grows up. Only then does she refuse and marry.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownerless property that anyone may take.
Until she grows up and reaches adulthood.

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל allow a קטנה to refuse many times. בית שמאי object that this treats Jewish girls like הפקר, so she must wait until she is grown before refusing and marrying.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
The daughters of Israel are not ownerless property,
rather, she refuses and waits
until she grows up,
and refuses, and marries.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: אֵין בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֶפְקֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers and rejects בית הלל's claim in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a קטנה may refuse and be married off again and again while still young.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Repeated marriages and refusals treat בנות ישראל like הפקר. Instead she must wait until she is grown, then refuse and marry.

steps.title: שמואל's reason for בית שמאי: no conditions in marriage
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that בית שמאי block מיאון for a married girl because people might wrongly conclude that a marriage can depend on a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What is the reason of בית שמאי? Because there are no conditions in a completed marriage. If a married girl could refuse, people would come to say that a marriage can have a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining why בית שמאי say a married קטנה cannot do מיאון. שמואל says the concern is about how it will look to the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A completed marriage (נשואין) cannot hang on a תנאי. When a girl does מיאון, the marriage falls away as if it never was, which looks like a marriage that depended on a condition. בית שמאי worry that people will copy this idea for adult marriages, so they limit מיאון to an ארוסה.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition attached to a marriage or deal
Completed marriage, the second stage after engagement

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying a married קטנה's marriage really has a condition. The worry is only that people watching will think so and apply it to adult marriages.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
What is the reason of Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: He means their ruling that only an engaged girl, not a married one, can do מיאון.

phrases.english: Because there are no conditions in marriage.
And if a married girl could refuse,
people would come to say there can be a condition in marriage.
phrases.notes: מיאון undoes the marriage, so it can look like the marriage hung on a condition all along.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis by giving the reason behind בית שמאי's position from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid מיאון for a נשואה so people will not think a marriage can have a תנאי.

steps.title: Challenge: what about a girl who entered the חופה but had no relations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל's reason fits a girl who entered the חופה but whose marriage was not yet consummated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she entered the חופה but did not have relations, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reason with a case where the marriage was not consummated. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule seems built on the idea that relations cannot be conditional. But a girl who only entered the חופה is already married even without relations. So why would בית שמאי still forbid her מיאון?

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: If she entered the wedding canopy and did not have relations,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests שמואל's reason against a marriage without relations.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reason that there is no תנאי בנישואין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is about relations not being conditional, a girl who only entered the חופה should not be included, yet בית שמאי still forbid her מיאון.

steps.title: Answer: a חופה also cannot be conditional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חופה itself, like relations, cannot have a תנאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there are no conditions in a wedding canopy either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by widening שמואל's rule. The חופה also cannot be conditional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not only about relations. Any completed marriage, including one done through חופה alone, cannot hang on a תנאי. So the same worry applies, and בית שמאי forbid מיאון here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Wedding canopy, the act that completes the marriage

phrases.english: Because there are no conditions in a wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין תְּנַאי בְּחוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The no-condition rule might only apply to relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The no-condition rule also applies to חופה, so the worry still exists.

steps.title: Challenge: what about a girl handed to the husband's agents?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a girl whose father handed her over to the husband's messengers, which counts as married even before any חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father handed her over to the husband's agents, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again with an even weaker case of marriage. It sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the father hands his daughter to the husband's agents, she counts as married even though there was no חופה and no relations. Here nobody would think of conditions in a חופה, so why would בית שמאי still forbid מיאון?

phrases.english: If the father handed her over to the husband's agents,
phrases.notes: Once she's handed over this way, she already counts as married, even before any חופה.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָסַר הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the חופה case was answered, a further case is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reason, even as widened to חופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this case there is neither relations nor חופה, so the no-condition worry seems not to apply.

steps.title: Answer: the Rabbis made one rule for all marriages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חכמים did not make distinctions; every kind of married girl is included in the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis did not distinguish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule covers every married girl, even in this unusual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the worry is weaker here, the חכמים set one clear rule for all married girls. They did not divide marriages into types, so a girl handed to the agents also cannot do מיאון according to בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis did not make a distinction; one rule for all cases

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, בית שמאי forbid מיאון for any married girl so people will not think marriage can be conditional. This covers relations, חופה, and even handing over to the husband's agents, because the חכמים made one rule.

phrases.english: The Rabbis did not distinguish.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא פְּלוּג רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the worry does not really apply here, she should be allowed to do מיאון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים made a single rule for all married girls, so she cannot.

steps.title: בית הלל's view: everyone knows a קטנה's marriage is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל are not worried by שמואל's concern, because people know a קטנה's marriage is only דרבנן and will not compare it to an adult's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? People know well that a minor girl's marriage is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בית הלל do not share בית שמאי's worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl married off as a קטנה by her mother or brothers is married only מדרבנן. Since everyone knows this, no one will learn from her מיאון that a real, Torah-level marriage can be conditional.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not Torah law

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel?
People surely know
that the marriage of a minor girl is only rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מִידָּע יָדְעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from בית שמאי to explain why בית הלל reject שמואל's concern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל allow a נשואה to do מיאון, since everyone knows her marriage is דרבנן and no wrong idea will spread.

steps.title: A different reason for בית שמאי: a man won't make his relations into זנות
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף give a different reason: once a man has relations with his wife, he does not want them to turn into forbidden relations through her מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: The reason of בית שמאי is that a man does not make his relations into relations of זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different explanation for בית שמאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון cancels the marriage from the start. Then the husband's past relations would turn out to be outside marriage, which is בעילת זנות. A man does not want that, so בית שמאי say a married girl cannot do מיאון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reason is about the husband's mindset, not about what the public might think. That is a different kind of reason from שמואל's.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
The reason of Beit Shammai
is that a man does not make
his relations into forbidden relations.
phrases.notes: If her מיאון undid the marriage, his past relations would end up having been outside marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason for בית שמאי, different from שמואל's in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid a נשואה's מיאון because a man does not want his relations to become בעילת זנות.

steps.title: What about a girl who entered the חופה but had no relations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason of רבה and רב יוסף with a case where there were no relations at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she went into the חופה but did not have relations with him, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given in step 13. That reason is about relations, so what about a girl who went into the חופה with no relations?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רב יוסף said the husband does not want his relations to become forbidden through her מיאון. But בית שמאי call her married as soon as she enters the חופה, even with no relations. Their reason does not seem to cover that case.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage canopy. Going into it makes her fully married (נשואה).
What can you say? A question showing the reason does not fit this case.

phrases.english: She entered the marriage canopy and did not have relations,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: He means: the reason about relations from step 13 doesn't fit here, so why can't she do מיאון?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְנְסָה לַחוּפָּה וְלֹא נִבְעֲלָה, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reason of רבה and רב יוסף from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the husband does not want his relations to become forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When there were no relations, there is nothing to become forbidden. Yet בית שמאי still forbid מיאון.

steps.title: He does not want a forbidden חופה either
steps.stepSummary: The husband does not want his חופה to turn into a forbidden חופה, even without relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not want it to turn out to be a forbidden חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same idea also covers the חופה. The husband does not want his חופה to become a forbidden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she could do מיאון later, the marriage would be undone from the start. Then he would have stood under a חופה with a woman who was not his wife. The husband does not want that, just as he does not want forbidden relations, so the reason still works.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not happy with it. He does not want it.

phrases.english: It is not acceptable to him
that it should be a forbidden marriage canopy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widens the reason to cover the חופה as well as relations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason only works where there were relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband also does not want a forbidden חופה, so the reason works even without relations.

steps.title: What about a father who handed her to the husband's messengers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again with a case where there was no חופה and no relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father handed her over to the husband's messengers, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second challenge. She counts as married once her father hands her to the husband's messengers, even with no חופה and no relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the husband has neither relations nor a חופה that could become forbidden. Yet she still counts as a נשואה, so by בית שמאי she cannot do מיאון. The reason from steps 13 and 15 does not seem to cover her.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same question the גמרא asked in step 10, but there it was asked against a different reason. Here the גמרא repeats it to test the reason of רבה and רב יוסף.

phrases.english: If the father handed her over to the husband's messengers,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the reason of רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the husband does not want a forbidden חופה or forbidden relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here there is no חופה and no relations at all, yet she still counts as married.

steps.title: The חכמים made one rule for every married girl
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not split up the cases of a married girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים did not make a difference between cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים made one rule for every married girl. They did not leave out the rare case of handing her to the messengers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason fits most marriages, which have a חופה and relations. Once the חכמים made a rule for married girls, they made it for every kind of married girl, so this case is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not make a difference between cases.

phrases.english: The Sages did not distinguish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The rule is made for every case of this kind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case covered by the rule must fit the reason behind it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers every married girl, even where the reason does not fully fit.

steps.title: How בית הלל answer this reason
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל say there is קדושין and a כתובה, so nobody will call his relations זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? Since there is קדושין and a כתובה, people will not say his relations were זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בית הלל do not accept the reason of רבה and רב יוסף. In their view, the relations will never look like זנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say the marriage was done the proper way, with קדושין and a כתובה. So even if she does מיאון later, nobody will think his relations were זנות. That means he has nothing to worry about, and she may still do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage.
Relations that are not part of a proper marriage.

steps.whatToRemember: By רבה and רב יוסף, בית שמאי forbid a married girl's מיאון so his חופה and relations do not become forbidden. בית הלל answer that with קדושין and a כתובה, nobody will call it זנות.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel?
Since there is betrothal and a marriage contract,
people will not come to say
that his relations were licentious relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא קִדּוּשִׁין וּכְתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's side of the reason from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With קדושין and a כתובה, the relations are never seen as זנות, so מיאון after marriage causes no problem.

steps.title: רב פפא: בית שמאי worry the husband will use up her property
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says both sides are about the profits from her property. בית שמאי worry that if she can leave, the husband will use them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל are thinking about the profits from her property. בית שמאי think that if a married girl can do מיאון, the husband will grab the profits and use them up, since she might leave him anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a whole new reason for the מחלוקת. It is about money, not forbidden relations. Here he explains בית שמאי's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband gets to eat the profits from the property his wife brings. If she can always leave by מיאון, he will not care for the property. He will just use up as much as he can while he has it. So בית שמאי say a married girl cannot do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: Profits from the wife's property, which the husband gets to use.
A fully married woman, after the חופה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The reason of Beit Shammai is because of profits,
and the reason of Beit Hillel is because of profits.
The reason of Beit Shammai is because of profits:
for if you say a married girl may refuse,
he will grab them from her and eat them up,
since in the end she is set to leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי מִשּׁוּם פֵּירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason of רבה and רב יוסף with a reason about money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By בית שמאי, letting a married girl do מיאון would lead the husband to use up her property's profits.

steps.title: רב פפא: בית הלל say the husband will take better care of her property
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל say the opposite: if she can leave, the husband will improve her property so her family won't pull her away.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say the opposite. Since she can do מיאון, he will take good care of her property. He thinks: if I don't, her relatives will push her to leave me and take her away.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב פפא's reason by giving בית הלל's side. They take the same money idea and turn it around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say the chance that she can leave makes the husband behave better. He will improve her property to keep her family happy, so they don't talk her into מיאון. So for them, letting her do מיאון helps her.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel: On the contrary,
since you say she may refuse,
he will surely improve them.
He thinks: if not,
her relatives will advise her,
phrases.notes: They will advise her to do מיאון and leave him.

phrases.english: and take her away from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פפא's reason with בית הלל's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By בית הלל, the chance of מיאון makes the husband take good care of her property.

steps.title: רבא: the wedding feast and making the marriage known
steps.stepSummary: רבא says בית שמאי worry a man won't pay for a wedding he could lose. בית הלל say both sides still want the marriage to be known.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is בית שמאי's reason. A man does not go to the trouble of a wedding feast just to lose it. And בית הלל say: Both of them still want it, so that people will hear they are married.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a fourth way to explain the מחלוקת. It is about whether people will still want to marry a קטנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say that if she could leave even after the wedding, no man would spend money on a feast for her. So they block מיאון after marriage. בית הלל say the marriage is still worth it to both sides, because everyone hears that they are married.

keyTerms.meaning: A feast, here the wedding feast.
Word getting around that they are married.

steps.whatToRemember: There are four explanations of the מחלוקת about a married girl's מיאון. שמואל says it is about people thinking marriage can have a תנאי. רבה and רב יוסף say it is about forbidden relations. רב פפא says it is about the profits of her property. רבא says it is about the wedding feast and making the marriage known.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is the reason of Beit Shammai:
A person does not bother with a feast and then lose it.
And Beit Hillel: It is good for both of them,
so that word will spread about them that they are married.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a fourth explanation of the מחלוקת, after שמואל, after רבה and רב יוסף, and after רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By בית שמאי, men won't marry a קטנה with a feast if she can still leave. By בית הלל, both sides gain from having the marriage known.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: she can refuse the יבם's מאמר but not the זיקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about מיאון toward a יבם. רבי אושעיא says she can refuse his מאמר but not the זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: בית שמאי say only against the husband, and so on. רבי אושעיא said: She can refuse his מאמר, but she cannot refuse his זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the משנה, about מיאון toward a יבם. רבי אושעיא sets a limit on what that מיאון can undo.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מאמר is the יבם's own קדושין to her, and her מיאון can cancel it. But the זיקה, the bond that ties her to the יבם, cannot be canceled by מיאון. So the מיאון toward a יבם only works on the מאמר.

keyTerms.meaning: A יבם's קדושין to the יבמה before ייבום, set up by the חכמים.
The bond tying a יבמה to her יבם.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: Against the husband, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: בית שמאי say מיאון works only against a husband, and בית הלל say also against a יבם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
She refuses his levirate betrothal,
but she does not refuse his levirate bond.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים בַּבַּעַל וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the second dispute of the משנה (step 2), about מיאון toward a יבם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה's מיאון can cancel a יבם's מאמר but not the זיקה itself.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks for רבי אושעיא's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks why רבי אושעיא makes a difference between מאמר and זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is רבי אושעיא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks a question to set up his own explanation. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. רב חסדא simply wants to know why מיאון works on one but not the other.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Oshaya?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does מיאון cancel a מאמר but not a זיקה?

steps.title: What she agreed to she can undo; what was forced on her she cannot
steps.stepSummary: The מאמר needed her agreement, so she can undo it. The זיקה came without her agreement, so she cannot undo it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מאמר, which happened with her agreement, she can undo. A זיקה, which happens even against her will, she cannot undo.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers his own question. The key is whether she agreed to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מאמר only works if she agrees, so her מיאון, which says 'I don't want this,' can undo it. The זיקה falls on her automatically the moment her husband dies, whether she wants it or not. Her saying 'I don't want it' has nothing to undo.
steps.whatToRemember: מיאון can only undo something that needed her agreement, like a מאמר. It cannot undo a זיקה, which falls on her whether she agrees or not.

phrases.english: A levirate betrothal, which is with her consent,
she can uproot.
A levirate bond, which is against her will,
she cannot uproot.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאֲמָר, דְּמִדַּעְתַּהּ — מָצְיָא עָקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her מיאון can undo something done with her agreement, like a מאמר, but not something forced on her, like a זיקה.

steps.title: But the יבם's ביאה can happen against her will
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 24 by pointing to ביאה, which can take place against the woman's will.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at ביאה, which can happen against her will!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a challenge to the rule it just gave. This line sets up the problem, and the next words finish the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said she can undo the מאמר because it needed her agreement, and she cannot undo the זיקה because it came without her agreement. But a יבם's ביאה also works even against her will. If her agreement is the test, ביאה should not be undoable by מיאון either, and that will clash with what the משנה teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at, yet here is. Opens a challenge.
Marital relations. Here, the יבם's act that completes יבום.
Against her will, without her agreement

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ביאה with מאמר. A מאמר needs her agreement, but ביאה completes יבום even against her will, and that is why it challenges the rule from step 24.

phrases.english: But look at ביאה,
phrases.notes: He means the יבם's ביאה, the act that completes יבום.

phrases.english: which can be against her will,

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי בִּיאָה, דִּבְעַל כֻּרְחַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 24, that her agreement decides whether she can do מיאון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 24: what needed her agreement can be undone by מיאון, and what came without her agreement cannot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביאה works even against her will, like זיקה. So by step 24's logic she should not be able to undo it by מיאון, which seems to clash with the משנה about מיאון toward a יבם. The rest of the challenge comes in the next words.
